NENYORK /ORD-TELEGRAM&SUN New York, New York December 6, 1954

Dr. Hockett Joins Tobacco Group

Industry ResearchCof. mittee. it was announced today byDr. ClarenceCook Little, scientific director.

Pr. Robert C. Hockett has beennamed an associate scientifie.director of the Tobaeco

Dr. Hockett will aid Dr. Little and the ScientificDr.R. C. Hockett

Advisory Board in developing the tobaceo industry's program of research into tobacco use and health, it was said. The committee recently made initial grantsof $82,000 to six institutions for basic research projects and is reviewing appllcations for additionalgrants. Dr. Hockett spent nine years prior to 1952 as scientific director of the Sugar Research Foundation.

VALL STREET JOURNAL New York, New York December 7, 1954

Tohacco Industry to Back Study

The committee plans to give a research grant to a group ofpathologists to conduct examinations of the bronchial system and the lungs. The data collected will be gathered at a central location for tabulating, comparing and analyzing. The group met here to discuss and plan the program, and will adopt specife plans at a later meeting.

NEW YORK—The tobacco industry's research committee expects to spend about $60.000 in the first year on a new project it's launching to study human lung ailments.

TobaccoResearch Aide Tobacco Research Aide Named

WASHINGTON, Dec. Dr. Robert C. Hockett pointedtodayassociate director ofthe Tobacco ResearchCommittee. Di ett, a native of Fayette, assist the committee in in tobacco use and hea Hockett untilrecently consultant. toArthurD Inc., and to pharmaceutt and beverage companies. formerassociateprofe chemistry at the Massa Institute ofTechnology. WASHINGTON, Dec. 5 (UP)— Dr. Robert C. Hockett wasappointedtodayassociate scientific director ofthe Tobacco Industry ResearchCommittee. Dr. Hockett, a native of Fayette, Mo., will assist the committee in research in tobacco use and health. Dr. Hockett until recently was a consultant, toArthur D. Little, Inc., and to pharmaceutical, food and beverage companies. He is a former associateprofessorof chemistryat the Massachusetts Instituteof Technology.
